test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.

(P) showcasing objects of historic, scientific and cultural interest

(Q) by taking us back in time

(R) museums are always

(S) treasure troves of information
solution:
The correct answer is** Option (3)** i.e. **RSPQ.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the subject "museums," which is correctly indicated by **part (R).**** **
 
• Following the subject, "are always" **(R)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear what museums are.
 
• **The next part,** "treasure troves of information showcasing objects of historic, scientific and cultural interest," starts the explanation about the museums, indicated by **(SP)**.
 
• **Ending with **"by taking us back in time" **(Q)** completes the sentence by stating the function of museums.

Therefore, the correct answer is **RSPQ.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (SPQR):** This option starts with "treasure troves of information showcasing objects of historic, scientific and cultural interest," which is incomplete and does not make sense grammatically.
 
• **Option 2 (PQSR):** This option starts with "showcasing objects of historic, scientific and cultural interest by taking us back in time," which makes the sentence incorrect as the explanation starts too early, missing contextual flow.
 
• **Option 4 (QSPR):** This option starts with "by taking us back in time treasure troves of information," which creates a fragmented and confusing sentence structure.
